name: Pan Ananapibut
detail: Fiscal Policy Office economist whose 2012 presentation titled "ภาษีความมั่งคั่ง" actually proposed a Korean-style property/land and building tax on housing above 5 million THB rather than a net wealth tax on total assets minus debt.

name: Sommai Phasee
detail: Finance Minister (2014–2015) who enacted the 2015 Inheritance Tax Act and Land and Building Tax Act; while frequently referred to in media as taxing the wealthy, these are inheritance and real property taxes excluded under Section 2.

name: Nitirat Sapsomboon
detail: Coordinator of We Fair Network. In his widely cited 2020 iLaw interview outlining tax funding mechanisms for universal welfare, he proposed capital gains tax (30%), progressive land and building tax, progressive inheritance tax, and cutting BOI privileges, but omitted an annual net wealth tax.

name: Somchai Jitsuchon
detail: Research Director for Inclusive Development at TDRI. While a leading academic voice on inequality and tax reform to finance pensions and child grants, his concrete proposals focus on land and building taxes, windfall taxes, capital gains taxes, and phased VAT increases, rather than an annual net wealth tax.

name: Lavaron Sangsnit
detail: Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance. Frequently cited in economic media discussing the structural flaws of the inheritance tax and noting that a net wealth tax (Wealth Tax) could be a future policy alternative; his comments represent administrative feasibility review and technical study rather than personal or institutional advocacy.

name: Pita Limjaroenrat
detail: Former Move Forward Party leader. While campaigning on the party's 2023 Progressive Welfare platform, his public statements focused broadly on welfare spending and economic revitalization; specific legislative drafting and direct defense of the net wealth tax was spearheaded by Sirikanya Tansakun and Think Forward Center, with no distinct standalone net wealth tax quote in his personal capacity.

name: Pasuk Phongpaichit
detail: Emeritus Professor of Economics at Chulalongkorn University and Thailand's foremost researcher on inequality. While her landmark research documents extreme wealth concentration, her concrete policy proposals advocate comprehensive personal income tax reform (taxing capital/property income equivalently to wage income), inheritance tax enforcement, and progressive land taxes, rather than an annual broad-based net wealth tax.

name: P-Move
detail: People's Movement for a Just Society (ขบวนการประชาชนเพื่อสังคมที่เป็นธรรม), the leading grassroots coalition representing peasants and urban poor networks. While campaigning against systemic inequality and land monopoly, its concrete legislative platform centers on the Progressive Land Tax Act (พ.ร.บ. ภาษีที่ดินอัตราก้าวหน้า) and the Land Bank Act (พ.ร.บ. ธนาคารที่ดิน), which are single-asset property taxes and excluded from the net wealth tax definition.

name: Pornchai Thiraveja
detail: Director-General of the Fiscal Policy Office (FPO / สศค.), Ministry of Finance. In May 2025, he outlined that the FPO is actively studying the design and feasibility of a Net Wealth Tax (ภาษีความมั่งคั่ง) to expand direct tax revenue; however, as a civil service agency head directing technical exploratory research without personal or political advocacy, this does not constitute policy advocacy under project standards.

name: Praipol Koomsup
detail: Emeritus Professor of Economics and former Dean of Economics at Thammasat University. In his May 2023 public policy analysis 'เก็บภาษีจากคนรวย เพื่อช่วยคนจน' (Taxing the Rich to Help the Poor), he evaluated international precedents for wealth taxes (France, Spain, Switzerland) and raised cautionary considerations regarding administrative complexity and the narrow wealth tax base in developing countries, without advocating implementation.

name: Nipon Poapongsakorn
detail: Distinguished Fellow and former President of the Thailand Development Research Institute (TDRI). Prolific researcher on inequality and fiscal policy who champions the reform of the Land and Buildings Tax (ภาษีที่ดินและสิ่งปลูกสร้าง) and inheritance tax to empower local government finance, rather than an ongoing net wealth tax.
